note: The geometry a brand may set, and the floors it may not. Three layers: the raw scales (--mds-space-*, --mds-radius-*, --mds-text-*) are the system's and are never re-pointed index-to-index, because a rung is shared by components that have nothing to do with each other; the roles below are the brand's, and a 'step' role must resolve to a rung while a 'length' role may state an off-grid px value, because three control heights are not a ladder and the number is the decision; the floors are nobody's. A role here is permanent public API — adding one is a minor bump, removing one is breaking — so the list grows only on a measured difference between a real brand and this one, never on a guess. The avatar scale is the shape of that rule: sm, md and lg are settable because an app asked for them, xs and xl are not because none did. Colour is settable in full — the template is colour — and its floor is a ratio rather than a name: the pairs in dsbridge/contract.json are held to their contrast by the tests beside it.

settable.why: The corner every card-shaped surface draws, and the first place a brand's softness reads.
The corner of a button, a field, and everything else the hand acts on.
The corner a photograph is cut to, which a brand often keeps squarer than its cards.
The top corners of a sheet rising off the bottom edge of the screen.
The corner of the small labelled shapes, where a 2px difference is still visible.
How far a screen's own content clears the chrome above and below it.
The gap between two things that belong to each other, such as a glyph and its label.
The rhythm between one section of a screen and the next.
The height of a control at the compact size, where a dense brand differs from a roomy one most.
The height of a control at the default size: the measure every form on the screen is built from.
The height of a control at the large size, where a touch-first brand takes more room.
The glyph inside a compact control; an icon set drawn on a 24px grid reads heavy at this step.
The glyph at the default size, which is the box a caller's icon is scaled into.
The glyph at the large size, where an icon stands on its own rather than beside a label.
The diameter of a circular icon-only button, which is its own decision rather than the height of the text controls beside it.
The drawn box of a checkbox and circle of a radio; the target around it is a floor, this is the mark.
The width of a switch's track, which sets how far the knob travels.
The height of a switch's track.
The moving knob; the difference between it and the track height is the inset around it.
The avatar beside a line of text, in a comment or a list row.
The avatar at the default size, in a card's byline.
The avatar on a profile, where the face is the subject rather than the label.
The height of the bottom bar, which is how much of a phone screen the chrome takes.

floors.why: 44px is the smallest target that ships. A brand that shrinks it takes the app away from the hands it was already hardest for.
The thickness of the keyboard focus ring, which is the only indication of where the keyboard is.
The gap between the ring and the control it surrounds, which is what keeps the ring visible on a filled surface.
The type inside an editable control: below 16px, iOS Safari zooms the page the moment the field takes focus.
The same floor at the compact size, which is where a reading scale would otherwise put 13px type.
The default size, floored through the role it aliases.
The large size, floored through the role it aliases.
